Where does AI fit?

Two places, and one hard question.

1Where it fits2Check it3Keep it on track
1 · Where it fits

AI fits in two places.

Two places · where an LLM earns its keep in an app

The chatbot
AI is the front door: you ask in words, it answers, or acts.

One · the chatbot, the front door

The glue between services
AI translates what one service gives back into what the next one needs.

Two · the glue between services

03

Part 3 of 3

How do you keep it
on track?

Leave less to chance.

1Where it fits2Check it3Keep it on track
3 · Keep it on track

Keep it on track

  1. 1Describe tool outputs
  2. 2Workflows
  3. 3Skills, as needed
  4. 4Memory outside

Make tools answer clearly.

One · the LLM and a tool, in a loop: call, response, decide

LLM
search_sales
search_sales(region: "North", week: 41) →
← response
The response
{ "id": "sr-1042",
  "w": 41, "r": "N",
  "v": 40960 }
? What is sr-1042? Is v dollars, or cents? Is r a region?

Raw fields · the names mean nothing to the model, so it guesses

Inputs · we already describe them
region: "North, South, East or West"
week:   "ISO week number, 1–53"

Inputs · we already describe what each parameter means

Outputs · describe them too
id: "this search; pass it to compare() to reuse it"
w: "ISO week" · r: "region: N = North"
v: "revenue, in dollars"

Outputs · describe them too: metadata the LLM reads with the data

compare("sr-1042", week: 40) →
← builds on it, doesn’t redo it

It uses the id · because it knows what the id is for

search_sales(region: "Nrth") →
← 400
When it fails · say what to do
400 · no region "Nrth" · valid: North, South, East, West  → fix it, retry
503 · busy  → retry in 30 s
404 · no data for week 41  → don’t retry; tell the user
403 · not allowed  → stop; ask for access

Errors · what was wrong, and what to do next: retry, wait, or stop

Without it · just “error”, and fields called v
It retries blindly, calls another tool, reads cents as dollars, or makes up an answer.
More calls, more time, and a guess at the end.

Without it · the LLM guesses, and wastes your time

With it · the answer
“Sales fell 20% in the North, $51,200 → $40,960 (sr-1042). I couldn’t find why.”
compare("sr-1042", week: 40) →
← week 40: $51,200 · week 41: $40,960

A better answer · the right numbers, its source, and honest about the gap

Same path? Make it a workflow.

1 · search_sales→2 · get_metrics→3 · compare→4 · send_email

every week: the same four tools, in the same order · four decisions, four chances to go wrong

weekly_report()one workflow, in code
search→metrics→compare→LLM · summarize→check→send

A workflow · code runs the path; the LLM writes the summary; a check before it’s sent

Deterministic where you can, an LLM where you must.

The rule · same input, same path

← data

weekly_report_skill() →

toolssearch_salesget_metricscompare

A skill · returns instructions, and the tools to follow them

What the LLM sees · at the start
weekly_report_skillsend_report_skillrefunds_skilljust the skill names, one line each
40 tools: hidden

weekly_report_skillsend_report_skillrefunds_skillsearch_salesget_metricscompareloaded on demand: the instructions,
and only the tools they need

Loaded on demand · calling a skill unlocks just its tools

send_report_skill() →
← instructions, and tools
What the LLM sees · next step
weekly_report_skillsend_report_skillrefunds_skillsend_emailnotifythe last step’s tools are gone;
the next ones come in
Progressive loading
The model sees what this step needs, and no more: three tools, then two.

Progressive · each step loads what it needs, and drops the rest

Fewer choices, fewer wrong ones.

The rule · fewer tools in view, fewer wrong picks
